name: Sukhothai Kingdom
summary: A Thai kingdom traditionally seen as the first Thai state. King Ram Khamhaeng is credited with the Thai script and Sukhothai with sangkhalok ceramics.

knownFor.label: Sangkhalok ceramics
knownFor.note: Glazed stoneware exported across Southeast Asia.

knownFor.label: Thai script
knownFor.note: Traditionally credited to King Ram Khamhaeng, though the inscription is debated.

knownFor.label: Walking Buddha statues
knownFor.note: A graceful new style of Buddha image unique to Sukhothai.

location.value: Northern central Thailand, centred on Sukhothai and later Song Khwae (Phitsanulok), with influence over much of the Chao Phraya basin under Ram Khamhaeng.
location.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

terrain.value: Flat river plains of the Yom and Nan rivers, tributaries of the Chao Phraya, ringed by low hills.
terrain.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

climate.value: Tropical monsoon climate with a long dry season, so the city built reservoirs and dykes to store water.
climate.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

resources.value: Rice land, forest products and good clay for the kilns of Si Satchanalai.
resources.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

disasters.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

population.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

urbanisation.value: Sukhothai was a walled city with moats, temples and reservoirs; Si Satchanalai was a twin city and pottery centre.
urbanisation.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

disease.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

migration.value: Tai-speaking peoples moved south into lands once ruled by the Khmer, settling the river valleys.
migration.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

economicBase.value: Rice farming plus a large ceramics industry; the famous inscription says trade was free of tolls.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

tradeRoutes.value: Exported sangkhalok ceramics across Southeast Asia.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

moneyAndTax.value: Cowrie shells and bent silver “bullet money” (photduang); the Ram Khamhaeng inscription says no tolls were charged on trade.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

inequality.value: King and nobles above commoners and slaves.
inequality.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

governmentType.value: A mandala kingdom with a paternal king (“father of the people”).
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

keyRulers.value: Si Inthrathit (founder, 1238), Ram Khamhaeng (1279–1298), Li Thai (Maha Thammaracha I, 1347–1368), Borommapan (last, d. 1438).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

succession.value: Hereditary within the Phra Ruang dynasty, though power passed between rival princes.
succession.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

institutions.value: A mandala system: the king ruled the core and received tribute from looser vassal towns.
institutions.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

stability.value: Strong under Ram Khamhaeng, but vassals broke away after his death; Ayutthaya invaded in 1349.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

eliteConflict.value: Vassal rulers and princes competed once the strong early kings died.
eliteConflict.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

armyAndTech.value: Armies of foot soldiers led by nobles riding war elephants.
armyAndTech.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

majorWars.value: Wars with Ayutthaya, which invaded in 1349.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

territoryChange.value: Greatest extent under Ram Khamhaeng; it shrank under pressure from Ayutthaya from the mid-14th century.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Ayutthaya and the Khmer; allied with Lan Na.
alliancesRivals.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

inventions.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

scienceEducation.value: Buddhist monasteries taught reading and religion; Li Thai wrote the Traiphum, a Buddhist cosmology.
scienceEducation.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

openness.value: Ties with Yuan China helped develop ceramics.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

religion.value: Theravada Buddhism of the Sri Lankan tradition, with older spirit beliefs.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

languageWriting.value: Thai script credited to Ram Khamhaeng (the inscription is debated).

artsArchitecture.value: Lotus-bud stupas, walking Buddha statues and temple ruins now in the Sukhothai Historical Park (UNESCO).
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

socialStructure.value: King and nobles, free commoners (phrai) and slaves.
socialStructure.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

sharedIdentity.value: A paternal Buddhist kingship: the king was described as a “father” to his people.
sharedIdentity.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

neighbours.value: The Khmer, Lan Na and Ayutthaya.
neighbours.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

ideasReligions.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

colonisation.source: Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

riseSignals.value: Si Inthrathit freed Sukhothai from Khmer control and founded the kingdom in 1238.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

peakPeriod.value: Under Ram Khamhaeng (1279–1298), when its influence reached far down the peninsula.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

declineSignals.value: Vassals broke away, and Ayutthaya invaded in 1349 and made Sukhothai a tributary from 1378.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

outcome.value: Annexed by Ayutthaya in 1438 after the death of Borommapan; its art and kingship ideas lived on in Ayutthaya.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Baker & Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (2014)

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Its role as “first Thai kingdom” is debated.
